transcript.content: [Rock music.]
XFM's Ricky Gervais talks to Bono.
I'm Ricky Gervais, and I'm talking to Bono off U2.
[As Bono] Hello there. Thanks for inviting me.
All right, Bono? Sorry, I don't know your surname.
I haven't got one.
Do you like XFM?
I bloody love it.
Is it because we play R.E.M., Eminem, Radiohead and Dr. Dre?
It is. And also, of course, you play some of my songs, U2 lead singer of. I've heard in the past on the station you've played "Pride in the Name of Love."
[Sings] Pride in the name of love-
[Singing together] Before you break my heart.
Love that one.
And I imagine Christmastime you'll probably be playing, um, "All Is Quiet on New Year's Day."
Oh, of course it is. All the shops are shut. There's no buses running.
That's what I wrote it about, Rick.
Thanks very much. Bono, I don't know your surname.
I haven't got one.
Ricky Gervais, this Saturday from one.
Yeah, with Steve Merchant. Just, you know, say that.
It's the Ricky Gervais Show.
With Steve Merchant.
Uh, we've got some great bands coming up. We've got Ash, R.E.M.—
Sure.
We've got Strokes, we've got Weezer, the usual stuff.
So listen, can I mention to you about the Aberdeen Angus Steakhouse?
Go on.
It's the one that you literally can see from this building.
Well, don't mention it.
What do you mean? There's loads of them.
No, but if they think you go there, then, you know, people will go there and we could charge them big advertising for that. We're losing revenue, you hand over fist.

No, we, um, I don't know if anyone's ever been in an Aberdeen Angus Steakhouse. For those that haven't really spotted them, they're those places that have always got the kind of red velvet seating, and they just like, it's just sometimes I think they're just called like a steakhouse.
Yeah.
So we went in there and we ordered the food, and I got to say this, the Aberdeen Angus Steakhouse, I'm embarrassed for the people that work there. They were embarrassed.
You can't say this.
No, it's not libellous. This is my opinion. It's like a restaurant review.
[Ricky laughs.]
It is. I'm like Michael Winner.
Oh, I'm gonna do that from now on as well. Write that one down, restaurant review, yeah, I can do that.
Yeah, but, um,
Got my film review coming up, don't forget that.
Oh, I look forward to that. But, um,
So we went in there and we ordered. I think my starter was prawns, right, in breadcrumbs.
Oh, that's the- that's the-
And I ordered them, and it-
That's the poshest thing you can do.
It was about four quid.
Four pounds.
Right, for prawns, right?
Imagine [unclear].
I swear to God, Rick, there were three prawns on a plate.
You're joking.
I'm not joking. Three prawns on a plate and a bit of grotty lettuce.
Oh my God.
It was shameful.
And they brought us— we ordered sort of steak or something. It's the worst place. Everything you've got to pay for. Napkins, salt and pepper, everything. It's ludicrous.
Seat hire.
It's absolu— it literally was awful, right? And there was about ten of us. It cost about two hundred quid.
You're joking.
I don't know what the meat was. I don't know...
Can I just say that is only twenty pounds each.
I don't think it was meat.
That is London.
I don't think it was meat. I think they'd literally crawled into the McDonald's next door. They were just stealing the meat waste from there.
Right.
It was unbelievable.
That is libelous, but it's obviously ironic. He's joking.

No, I'm not saying— I'm saying that this is my hypothesis, Rick. It was an absolute travesty. I don't know how they get away with it. I don't know who goes back there. I thought restaurants were building a reputation on people who return and eat again.
And as you say, it's probably American tourists.
I like the way they look like a bingo hall. Because you're walking past, it's huge, with a big opening. You can see exactly who's eating there from the beginning,
To- do you know what I mean? From the-
Yeah.
And it's always like a couple of parents and some kids who are obviously not enjoying themselves.
Yeah, they're fat kids as well.
Especially if they're about fourteen.
I know, yeah. Yeah. Yeah.
And.
After the Aberdeen Angus Steakhouse, we were very annoyed. And as is obviously the tradition on a stag night, it was, well, we must have— we'd have to go to a strip club.
Right.

Now, I'm not a fan of that sort of thing, I have to say, unlikely as that may seem. And I've never been to one before. And we tried to get in Stringfellows, but it's like twenty quid to get in. And it's like, yeah, we'd like to see naked ladies, not that much.
Yeah.
So we went up to— I think it's called— is it Raymond's Revuebar? Do you know the one I mean? It's sort of— I think it's Berwick Street or something.
Right.

And we go in there, and there's like ten of us and we're all dressed up and that. We all sort of come on in, and we go, “How much is it for the show?” And he goes, “Uh, it's a tenner each for an hour-long show. Various ladies, uh, stripping. Um, but it has already started.”

And I went, oh, I'm not sure I want to come in now, I'm sure I won't be able to pick up the plot. And he just looked at me like, yeah, you obviously want to see the naked ladies, just come in, pay your money, keep your mouth shut.

There was no place for humour in there. So we go in, and it's not as seedy as you might think. It's actually, it's quite, quite nice in there. It's always, it's quite tasteful. It hasn't changed since about 1965, but it's okay.

It's all, rather like the Aberdeen Angus Steakhouse, it's not dissimilar to one of those inside. So uh, the show's already begun and, uh, and these girls come on and uh, on the outside it says all nude girls and there's a bloke, I swear, at the back.
As the girl came on, he went, get him off!
I think that's guaranteed, to be honest.
Yeah.

So what was great about it was there was a kind of a voice that announced each particular girl as she came on. And she, it was so, it was so awful and camp and just ludicrous. I actually dozed off at one point.

It's so boring, 'cause you— there's not much— many surprises. If you've seen one girl naked, they're all pretty much the same. There's no erotic tattoos or anything, or a slideshow hidden down there. There's nothing. So— no puppetry. You know what I mean? It's just the same old thing.
So, um, so there's this voice that comes on before each girl, and it introduces her name and they've all got amazing names. There was, uh, Scorpio Rising.
Vanity Fair! Passionara Fighter! And Passionara Fighter was a girl who kind of came on straddled— they all had props. And she was straddling, like, a kind of anti-aircraft gun.
Right.
Which is possibly the least erotic thing you can have. And as she was taking her clothes off, she sort of flung her bra—
See, that sounds a bit phallic to me.
Well, I imagine it was phallic.
I've studied Freud.

And, uh, she threw her bra off, right, and it sort of— and it fell behind her. And it's a very small stage and there's curtains at the back, and this— it's very hard to be erotic when, as you see a girl's brassiere fall behind, you just see a pole with a hook on it appear from the curtains and drag it back in. And you can just see through the crack of the curtains some guys that look like when Eric Morecambe and Ernie Wise, you know, when they were trying to put—

—that shoe back on Shirley Bassey in their classic show, where they're wearing those brown coats. It was like that. Two blokes in there. But I've never been in one before and I shall never go in again. It's like, it's— I've done it now.
I've done the Aberdeen Steakhouse, the paintballing and the strip club. That's it.
Yeah.
Three things I had to do in life before I died.
Swim with the dolphins?
Take a shower is the next one. And kiss a girl.
Saw a... interesting thing last night.
Go on.
It was a repeat of, um, The Priory, with that- you know that James Harries?
Who's James Harries?
You know, um... Oh God, there's a... er, this guy who was, um, he was about ten and he was on the, the Wogan show talking about antiques, and he's like-
Oh, is he like a kind of curly-haired-?
Yeah, he's that little- little freak boy talking about, "Oh, er, er, antiques, they have to shout to you." And, er, and then he's on The Priory and he's had a sex change.
Has he?
Yeah. Yeah, he looks a bit like a young Mavis Riley now.
He's not still ten though?
No.
No.
No, he's twenty or something.
Yeah, sure.

And, er, and they were talking about it and, er, and they showed the clip of, um, the Wogan thing, and... and there's a bit in it that goes, er, "Wonderful little boy, special little kid. I wonder what you'll be like when you're twenty."
Steve laughs.

And I just think, "Well, Terry, I certainly won't have a cock. I can tell you that much." But it was great because at one point in The Priory, going, "Yeah," he's going, "You were a funny little fellow, weren't you?" He goes, he was- oh, he was embarrassed. He was going, "Oh yeah," he said. He said, "I was worried 'cause at one point I thought I was gay."
Phew! That was avoided then.
Yeah.
I found out after I left school one of the kids I was at school with had had a sex change, right? And, er, um, a mutual friend, this is how he broke the news to me. He came in one day-
This wasn't the- was this- wasn't the person who had the operation?

No, no, no. This was another friend. He was a sort of mutual friend of ours, but he wasn't a big friend. We sort of knew him. He was in our, our year. And, er, my mate came round once and went, "Oh yeah," he said, "er, have, er, you seen Darren, er, Ripley, er, lately?" I went, "Er, no. No, what's he doing?" He went, "He's got a lovely little pair of tits."
Steve laughs.
That's how- I went, "What?" But isn't that a great way to break the news? "You seen, er... lovely little pair of tits."
Did you, did you, did you meet him then, the, the sex change guy?
No.
Did you ever see him afterwards?
No, no. I haven't seen him for, you know, twenty years. But-
I wonder if, 'cause I'd like- I'm kind of intrigued now to know if he has got-
Imagine that, imagine that. Breaking it to your mum. "All right?" "Hello, yeah. How was university?" "Good, good. Can I borrow your bra?"
Steve laughs.
I like- I-
I'm not sure I'd have had a tiny little pair of tits. I'd have had some big Jordan-style ones if I had a sex change operation.
Ricky laughs.
'Cause then I can get- no, 'cause then, you know, it's sort of, it's, it's a novelty, innit? I'd get in the paper.
Oh God. Well, what you could do is you- you could have your bollocks inflated. You could have them removed and go, "Er, doctor, don't throw them away."
Yeah, I've got a-
Don't throw them away.
-I've got a plan for them.
Yeah, go on. What are you thinking? What are you thinking?
I'm just thinking in the chestal area.
Oh yeah. What, inflate the bollocks that are already there?
Ideally, yeah. Could you attach some nipples?
Oh.
Fake or otherwise.
You could, you could utilise the penis as well, couldn't you?
What would that be for?
Well, it'd be a... well-
An interesting pendant?
Ricky and Steve laugh.
Yeah!

Alright.

Right.

I can see you veering towards staying in, Karl. What will you be watching on telly tonight?
Well, Jonathan Ross is on tonight, BBC One. He's got Ian Brown and Noel Gallagher in.
Gallagher, always value for money. Um, Oh, something for you, your favourite on Channel 5, Cosmetic Surgery.
What's that about?

Oh, maybe you won't like it. Designer Vaginas. Insight into the issue of genital enhancement. I mean, genital en— what— who goes along to have that sorted out? What experience have they had of people telling them, “Oh, June, you've got to get that minge sorted out. It's rubbish”?
Surely you'd have work done on your face before you worry about what's going on down there.
Well, no, their face is probably alright.
Well, what's up with their minge?
I don't know, I haven't seen it.

If you wanna go to the theatre, um, One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest is in town, starring Christian Slater and my mate Mackenzie Crook. That's on at the Gielgud Theatre. Knowing you, Karl, you'll be, uh, staying in and watching telly tonight?
Something good tonight, Channel 4, 8:05. Er, Tony Robinson presents Worst Jobs in History, right? One of 'em being about a fella whose job it was to wipe the arse of Henry VIII.
Right.
How bad is that? I mean, is anyone that busy that they haven't got time?
I don't know!
And how does it- does, does someone have to go for a job interview to get that job?
[Ricky laughs.]

Super Size Me, that's out this weekend.
It's like that bloke who ate nothing but fast food for a month, innit? And put on a lot of weight. There's a surprise.

Rik Waller said, “Are you gonna leave that?”
Channel 5 tonight at 8, er, truth about the killer squid.

I just...
He wasn't a wizard, was he?

Ross Noble's still on at the Apollo Theatre. He's great. He makes it all up as he goes along. Not like us, brilliantly scripted stuff.
Yeah. Anyway, over on the National Geographic channel, eight o'clock, brilliant programme. It's called, Cleverest Ape in the World.
Yeah.
Yeah? And what it's about is this- this ape, right, that's working with a scientist, and, er, they do some maths tests together and that, and the ape manages to sort of outdo the- the scientist.

Stood at the back watching.
The only thing swinging round him were his old, saggy bollocks. And why are we talking about a programme that was on a week ago?
Oh. If you want to know what's on tonight, look in the Guide.
